newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam has room for 2-3 refineries by 2010.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam has room for 2-3 refineries by 2010.

text.p: Vietnam's large appetite for energy related products justifies the building of as many as three refineries and a series of petrochemical plants by 2010, a senior Petrovietnam official said on Monday.

"The forecast results of the petroleum and petrochemical products of Vietnam's demand in the period 2000-2010...(justify) at least two or three refineries with the total processing capacity of 18-20 million tonnes of crude per year," Pham Anh Tuan, an official at Petrovietnam's oil and gas processing department said.
He was speaking to a refining conference in Singapore.
Demand for oil products for the year 2000 is projected to rise to 8.55 million tonnes, almost double 1994's consumption of 4.753 million tonnes, Pham said.
By the year 2010, oil product demand was estimated at 17.02 million tonnes with ethylene demand projected at 850,000 tonnes, from the current zero base.

To meet part of the increase in demand, Petrovietnam is expected to start up a 6.5 million tonne per year (130,000-barrel-per-day) crude unit by the middle of 2000 at Dung Quat Bay, in central Vietnam.
Pham said the new refinery would process 5.5 million tonnes of domestic sweet crude and 1.0 million tonnes of imported sour crude.
The US$1.3 billion refinery would also be fitted with complex secondary units such as fluid catalytic cracker and residue catalytic cracker to maximise diesel and gasoline production, he said.
By the year 2000 Vietnam's gasoline and diesel demand is projected to reach 2 million tonnes and 4.16 million tonnes, respectively.

Pham said the choice of Dung Quat Bay in central Quang Ngai province was based on Vietnam's long-term national development plan for the area and the area's natural attributes which suited a deep water port.
